lawyer: Mr. A.K. Mujibur Rahman -- for the Contemner-Opposite-Party.
parties:
Kurigram District Judgeship ----- Petitioners
Versus
Mr. Md. Abdul Huq, Deputy Commissioner, Kurigram ----- Contemner-Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
2. It is alleged that the contemner the then Deputy Commissioner, Kurigram, sent letters to different agencies including the Supreme Court of Bangladesh informing the alleged conspiracy hatched up by the judicial officers of the District including the District Judge in the matter of convicting and sentencing him to suffer 3 months Civil Jail and a fine of Tk. 5000/-in Misc. Case No. 31/94 for willful disobedience of Court's Order. The allegations against the judicial officers of the District including the District Judge are not only objectionable but also lowered down the image of the Court by sending its copy to different agencies of the Government. The contemner Mr. Abdul Haque, was allergic towards the judicial judgment affect in his interest and try to disobey the Court's order out of vanity and hot headiness treating the Court's Order as his personal loss and interest. 

 3. The sole contemner opposed the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition alleging inter alia that he contested the suits in order to safeguard the interest of the Government as per charter of duty of Deputy Commissioner. He further alleged that one Hazrat Ali got ex-parte decree in title suit No.680 of 1994 against Government in respect of undemarcated 7.00 acres of land out of 17.93 acres on the basis of some antedated and forged papers and that the said plaintiff again filed another suit for permanent injunction a few years thereafter against the Government and also filed a case for alleged violation of Court's temporary injunction which according to him (the contemner) does not lie. Incidentally he also alleged that the said Hazrat Ali met him in his bungalow and reported that he had been forced to file the said violation case and an affidavit to that effect was also sworn in but the said Hazrat Ail filed another affidavit alleging that the contemner forcibly obtained the said affidavit. The contemner respondent also alleged that he did not tender any mercy petition in the said violation case but a petition was filed by using his name for which he sent petition to different agencies including the Sheristader of the concerned Court describing the conspiracy hatched up against him. He thereafter alleged that he being president of the local Shilpakala Academy did not allow elected committee to take over charge since he was not held properly and for which a suit was filed an Advocate and a case for violation of Court's Order was also filed against which an appeal is pending. The upshot of the submissions of the contemner respondent is that some interested persons backed by the local judicial officers implicated him in different suits/cases in order to lower down his prestige-since he tried to protect the Government as well as public interest and the acts done by the definitely come under the charter of duties of Deputy Commissioner as enunciated by the Government. Accordingly he prayed for exoneration from the charge by discharging the Rule. 

 4. We have heard Mr. A.K. Mujibur Rahman, the learned Advocate for contemner who took us through the affidavit-in-opposition and the charter of duty of Deputy Commissioner as framed by the Government. The learned Advocate for the contemner submitted that his client reported the step-motherly attitude of the local judicial officers towards him to the different authorities explaining his position and to safeguard the interest of the Government and contended that the same in no way comes under the mischief of contempt of Court. He also submitted that his client never willfully violated the Court's Order in as much as he explained his position by sending a copy of letter, to the Sheristader of the concerned Court in order to avoid all future complicacies. 

 6. From the plain reading of the affidavit-in-opposition as well as from sub-mission of the learned Advocate for the contemner it is crystal clear that some suits and cases brought to light against the contemner due to his some action. Incidentally it may be noted here that the learned Advocate for the contemner submitted that the learned Sessions Judge. Kurigram became since the local Magistrate disposal of the case under Section 156(8) of the Customs Act which involved a Paul sum at his (contemner) instance on the basis of a circular issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs on that behalf. The affidavit-in-opposition also reflects the same. In reply to this we may simply say that the contemner ignored the correct position of law since circular car not override the substantive law Moreover, there is no paper to show that the same was exclusively charge-sheet.ec under Custom Act. It is from our experience that now a days the cases uncle Section 156(8) of the Customs Act tagged with Special Powers Act which is the correct position of law and if so, how Magistrate is competent to dispose of suet, cases since he is not authorised to hold trial under Special Powers Act. Be the case as it may, we are unable to make our comment on this subject for want of paper; that behalf but we are convinced that the remark of the Sessions Judge about competency of the Magistrate to try and dispose of such cases has annoyed the contemner since the authority enquired into and asked for the explanation in this regard from the contemner. The trial and disposal of criminal cases is done as per law and law will take US own course. Any one including Government is at liberty to seek redress by way of appeal or revision if aggrieved by the decision of any court. The Sessions Judge has obligation to see that the forum and procedure of a Criminal trial is being followed as per law within his Sessions Division. So in our opinion the Sessions Judge committed no illegality by sending copy of judgment arid order sheet of a particular case to the concerned Ministry holding that the same was riot tried and disposed of in accordance with law. We are sure that the same has hit the vanity of the contemner as the said Ministry may have asked for his explanation. 

 8. It appears that the contemner remained consciously silent; about the allegations of disobeying the Court's order in Title Suit No. 5/94 for permanent injunction and T.S. No. 105 of 1994 for handing over charge to the newly elected members of the Shilpakala Academy. However the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the contemner bears some attempt to justify the act of disobeying the order of temporary injunction in T.S. No.105 of 1994 on the ground of non-specification of the suit land but remained silent as to the alleged violation of order of temporary injunction passed in T.S. No. 105 of 1994. Be the case as it may, we refrain from making any comment about the same since both the subjects are sub-judice matters. However, we may recall that the contemner admitted in his affidavit-in-opposition that Hazrat Ali the plaintiff of Title Site No. 5/94 met him in his bunglow and allegedly reported that the concerned Assistant Judge persuaded him to file a case for violation of order and swore an affidavit. on that behalf. On the other hand, it appears from the report of the District Judge that the contemner man-aged to obtain affidavit from the plaintiff by force and the said plaintiff filed affidavit denying the allegations of the contemner. It. also appears from the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the contemner that he reported the matter to different authorities including the Sheristader of the concerned Court in order to explain his position. The visit of official b'unglow of the contemner by the litigant public (plaintiff of T.S. No. 5/94) and correspondence .by the contemner with the Sheristader of Civil Court for alleged clarification of the position of the contemner speaks much about his mentality which proves what type of man he is the visit of the Banglow of the contemner by a litigant public and correspondence with the Sheristader speaks much about his standard and as such no great thing can be expected from him. The misbehaviour of the contemner with the judicial officers of the station and sending of different allegations against them to different authorities to lower down the prestige of the judicial officers in order to hide his own guilt should not be allowed to go unnoticed. 

 9. This kind of behaviour and standard of the contemner who happens to the executive head of the Government in the district should not be allowed to continue and action should be taken in iron hand in order to save the image of the Government. In this connection we may quote the observation of their lordships in the case of State Vs. Abdul Karim Sarker 7 DLR 34 where it was observed that the executive arm of the Government should not be allowed to attack and defame the honour, dignity, majesty and independence of the judicial organ of the State. If they are allowed then in no time the remaining civilised fabric of our society will collapse. The executive branch of the Government to which the contemner belong is completely distinct from judiciary and the former has no mariner of super-vision or control over the judicial officers and the Government has in no conferred any authority to the contemner in the case of duty of the Deputy Commissioner except preferring appeal or revision, against the judgment and order of any Court if the Government interest is hampered and nothing else. So, the reporting by the contemner about the local Judicial officers to the different agencies of the Government are exfacie illegal and for which he must pay. The reporting by the contemner to the authorities against the local judicial officers are considered to malign the latter (Judicial officers) which comes under the mischief of contempt of Court and this kind of unwarranted activities of the contemner should not be allowed to go unpunished, otherwise there will be anarchy and hooliganism between the different branch of the administration and thereby the image of the Government will be at stake.
